title: Comparative evaluation of functional and patient-reported (subjective) parameters before and after combined orthodontic and orthognathic treatment.
summary:
This study investigates how jaw surgery affects patients with jaw misalignment (dentofacial deformities) in terms of their quality of life and lower jaw mobility.
These conditions can lead to functional limitations, difficulties in chewing, and reduced quality of life.
Patients are assessed before and after surgery. The study evaluates how well they can move their lower jaw and how they rate their quality of life. In addition, objective measurements of jaw movement are performed using a digital recording system.
The aim is to determine whether patients improve after surgery and whether changes in jaw mobility are related to changes in quality of life.
conditions: Dysgnathie (skelettale Fehlstellungen der Kiefer, z. B. Angle-Klasse II und III)

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient proficiency in German to independently complete a questionnaire
- Planned orthognathic surgery (monomaxillary or bimaxillary osteotomy) as part of a combined orthodontic-surgical treatment
- or planned orthognathic surgery (monomaxillary or bimaxillary osteotomy) in the context of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS)
Exclusion criteria:
- Minor patients (under 18 years of age)
- Patients who are unable to independently complete a questionnaire due to insufficient German language proficiency
- Lack of informed consent
- Surgery not performed
- Incomplete or non-evaluable datasets/questionnaires
